<doc title="Model Card and Config Validation" path="02-architecture/model-card-and-validation.md">
# Model Card and Config Validation

## Why the card is the source of truth

The platform needs to know three things before it can run a model: what
parameters it accepts, what files it reads, and what it writes. In EPISERVE those
are declared once in `fdo.json`, the **model card**, which follows the
[model-card v1 spec](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/episerve_specs/blob/main/src/episerve_specs/specs/model_card/README.md)
([`fdo.json:1-7`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L1-L7)).

The card is not documentation that happens to be machine-readable; it is the
input to the validator. `config_schema.py` loads `episerve:parameters` from the
card and hands it to `jsonschema`
([`src/config_schema.py:38-72`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/config_schema.py#L38-L72)).
Changing a bound in the card changes what the API server accepts, what
`--check-config` accepts, and what the tests assert — without touching Python
logic.

| Card section | Consumer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `episerve:task` | API server, benchmark workflow | [`fdo.json:18-29`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L18-L29) |
| `episerve:parameters` | `config_schema.validate_config` | [`fdo.json:31-67`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L31-L67) |
| `episerve:inputs` | runner preflight | [`fdo.json:69-92`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L69-L92) |
| `episerve:outputs` | runner postflight, scoring | [`fdo.json:94-109`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L94-L109) |
| `episerve:resources` | Kubernetes Job spec | [`fdo.json:111-117`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L111-L117) |
| `episerve:documentation` | catalog / model page | [`fdo.json:119-127`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L119-L127) |

## Validation flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Card as fdo.json
    participant CS as config_schema
    participant V as Draft202012Validator
    participant Run as run.main

    Run->>CS: validate_config(config)
    CS->>Card: read_text()
    CS->>CS: json.loads
    CS->>CS: check_schema(parameters)
    alt card invalid
        CS-->>Run: SchemaError
    else card valid
        CS->>V: Validator(parameters)
        V-->>CS: iter_errors(config)
        CS->>CS: _describe each error
        CS->>CS: fill defaults
        CS-->>Run: (resolved, errors)
    end
```

<!-- Sources: src/config_schema.py:38-134 -->

The two error classes are deliberately distinct:

| Exception | Meaning | Who fixes it |
|---|---|---|
| `SchemaError` | The card is missing, not JSON, or not a valid JSON Schema | Maintainer |
| validation errors | The user's `config.json` is wrong | Caller |

`run.py` reports them differently: a card problem says *"model card (fdo.json)
parameters are invalid"*, a config problem prints each user-facing message
([`src/run.py:74-82`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/run.py#L74-L82)).

## The parameter schema

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Parameters {
        type: object
        required: [history_length, prediction_length]
        additionalProperties: false
        rules: list
    }
    class HistoryLength {
        type: integer
        minimum: 3
        unit: steps
    }
    class PredictionLength {
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 512
    }
    class PredictionOffset {
        type: integer
        minimum: 0
        default: 0
    }
    class Statistic {
        type: string
        enum: [mean, median, last]
        default: mean
    }
    Parameters --> HistoryLength
    Parameters --> PredictionLength
    Parameters --> PredictionOffset
    Parameters --> Statistic
```

<!-- Sources: fdo.json:31-67 -->

Two details are worth calling out:

- **`additionalProperties: false`** makes unknown keys an error. This is why a
  typo such as `history_lenght` fails loudly instead of silently using the
  default ([`fdo.json:34`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L34)).
- **`rules`** is not JSON Schema; it is a list of human-readable cross-field
  constraints that `run.py` enforces after loading data
  ([`fdo.json:63-66`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L63-L66)).

## How errors become readable

`_describe` maps `jsonschema` error objects to one-line messages keyed by the
offending parameter
([`src/config_schema.py:75-99`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/config_schema.py#L75-L99)):

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    E["jsonschema error"] --> V{"validator"}
    V -- required --> R["missing required key"]
    V -- additionalProperties --> A["unrecognised key(s)"]
    V -- type --> T["must be a/an <type>"]
    V -- minimum --> M["must be >= n"]
    V -- maximum --> X["must be <= n"]
    V -- enum --> N["must be one of ..."]
    V -- other --> O["raw message"]
    R --> S["sorted, one line per error"]
    A --> S
    T --> S
    M --> S
    X --> S
    N --> S
    O --> S

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class E,V,R,A,T,M,X,N,O,S dark
```

<!-- Sources: src/config_schema.py:75-99 -->

Errors are sorted by path so that two runs with the same bad config produce the
same output order
([`src/config_schema.py:121-125`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/config_schema.py#L121-L125)).
That is what makes the CLI output testable.

## Defaults

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["config dict"] --> B{"key declared?"}
    B -- yes --> C["keep value"]
    B -- no --> D{"default in card?"}
    D -- yes --> E["use default"]
    D -- no --> F["omit from resolved"]
    C --> G["resolved"]
    E --> G
    F --> G

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class A,B,C,D,E,F,G dark
```

<!-- Sources: src/config_schema.py:127-134 -->

`resolved` always contains every declared key that has a value or a default. For
this card, a minimal `{"history_length": 3, "prediction_length": 1}` resolves to
all four keys, with `prediction_offset=0` and `statistic="mean"`
([`tests/test_config_schema.py:68-77`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/tests/test_config_schema.py#L68-L77)).

## Card validation in CI

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P["push / PR"] --> C["job: model-card"]
    C --> A["The-EPISERVE-Consortium/episerve_specs@v0.4.0"]
    A --> R{"valid?"}
    R -- yes --> OK["green check"]
    R -- no --> ERR["red check, image still builds"]

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class P,C,A,R,OK,ERR dark
```

<!-- Sources: .github/workflows/publish.yml:18-24 -->

The card job is independent of `build-and-test`, so an invalid card is visible
but does not block a code fix from shipping
([`.github/workflows/publish.yml:18-21`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml#L18-L21)).
Locally:

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/episerve_specs@v0.4.0"
episerve-validate fdo.json
```

## Parameter roles

`episerve:task.parameterRoles` tells the benchmark workflow which parameters to
prefill from the dataset split
([`fdo.json:24-28`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L24-L28)):

| Role | Parameter | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `horizon` | `prediction_length` | test-window length |
| `history` | `history_length` | history window |
| `offset` | `prediction_offset` | back-test gap |

Without this mapping the workflow would have to special-case every model's
parameter names.

<doc title="Build Your Own Model" path="03-template/build-your-own-model.md">
# Build Your Own Model

## Why this repository is a template

Most of an EPISERVE model is not the model. It is the adapter between the
platform and a forecasting method: reading `/work`, validating the card,
slicing the history window, extrapolating the time axis, filling gaps, writing
the TSV, and passing CI. This repository implements that adapter in about 540
lines and keeps the actual forecast in one small module (116 lines)
([`src/model.py:49-116`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/model.py#L49-L116)).

That split is the template: **keep the adapter, replace the core**. A more
sophisticated method — gradient boosting, a transformer, a state-space model —
changes `src/model.py` and the card, not the container contract.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Adapter["Platform adapter (keep)"]
        R["run.py<br>I/O, window, exit codes"]
        C["config_schema.py<br>card validation"]
        S["series.py<br>axis, gaps"]
    end
    subgraph Core["Core method (replace)"]
        M["model.py<br>forecast()"]
    end
    R --> C
    R --> M
    M --> S
    M --> O["predictions.tsv"]

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class R,C,S,M,O dark
```

<!-- Sources: src/run.py:25-26, src/model.py:15, src/config_schema.py:102 -->

## Keep / replace

| Path | Action | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `src/run.py` | Keep | The container contract, window slice and error format |
| `src/config_schema.py` | Keep | The card is already a JSON Schema; don't duplicate it |
| `src/series.py` | Keep | Axis inference and the gap policy are dataset-agnostic |
| `src/model.py` | **Replace** | This is the method |
| `tests/test_run.py` | Keep, extend | Locks the CLI contract |
| `tests/test_series.py` | Keep | Locks axis and gap behaviour |
| `tests/test_config_schema.py` | Keep, extend | Ties the card to the code |
| `tests/test_model.py` | **Replace** | Tests for your method |
| `fdo.json` | Edit | Name, parameters, I/O, resources, documentation |
| `Dockerfile`, `requirements*.txt` | Edit | Your runtime and dependencies |
| `.github/workflows/publish.yml` | Keep | Card check, in-image tests, GHCR |
| `documentation/` | Edit | Keep the pages truthful |

Source: [`src/`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/tree/main/src),
[`tests/`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/tree/main/tests).

## The core contract

Your replacement must keep this shape
([`src/model.py:49-55`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/model.py#L49-L55)):

```python
def forecast(
    x_series: pd.Series,      # history x, already sliced
    y_series: pd.Series,      # history target, may contain NaN
    prediction_length: int,   # H
    row_offset: int = 0,      # absolute row index of the first history row
    **parameters,             # declared in fdo.json
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ...
```

`row_offset` is the absolute row index of the first history row. Pass it to
`future_values` for a string axis, so `x_auto_converted` is absolute in the
input file rather than relative to the window.

and this output
([`src/model.py:103-114`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/model.py#L103-L114)):

| Column | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<x>` (input name) | yes | Future time value |
| `x_auto_converted` | only string axis | 1-indexed absolute row position (uses `row_offset`) |
| `<y>` (input name) | yes | Point forecast |
| `<y>_q10` | yes | Lower quantile |
| `<y>_q90` | yes | Upper quantile |

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Run as run.py
    participant Core as your forecast()
    participant Series as series.py

    Run->>Run: slice window [start:end]
    Run->>Core: x_series, y_series, H, parameters
    Core->>Series: prepare_target(y) if needed
    Core->>Series: future_values(x, H)
    Series-->>Core: future x values
    Core->>Core: fit / predict / quantiles
    Core-->>Run: DataFrame with x, point, q10, q90
    Run->>Run: write predictions.tsv
```

<!-- Sources: src/run.py:121-145, src/model.py:89-114 -->

The invariants that make the adapter work:

| Invariant | Consequence if broken |
|---|---|
| No file, network or clock access in the core | Tests need the platform; runs become non-reproducible |
| Same input + config → same output | Benchmark comparisons are meaningless |
| `q10 <= point <= q90` | Scoring rejects or penalises incoherent intervals |
| One row per step, exact column names | Runner postflight and scoring fail |
| Never read beyond the history window | Future leakage inflates the score |
| Respect `maxHorizon` | Memory/runtime blow-up in the Job |

Source: [`fdo.json:94-108`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L94-L108),
[`src/model.py:76-97`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/model.py#L76-L97).

## Swapping in a sophisticated method

A realistic replacement keeps the interface and moves all complexity behind it.
The example below is pseudocode for a gradient-boosted, recursive one-step model;
the point is the shape, not the algorithm:

```python
def forecast(x_series, y_series, prediction_length, row_offset=0, **params):
    values = prepare_target(y_series)          # reuse series.py
    future, positional = future_values(x_series, prediction_length)
    if positional:
        future = [value + row_offset for value in future]

    model = load_booster(params["model_path"])  # baked into the image
    history = list(values)
    rows = []
    for step in range(prediction_length):
        features = make_features(history, step, params)
        point = float(model.predict(features)[0])
        q10, q90 = residual_quantiles(model, features, params)
        rows.append(row(future[step], point, q10, q90))
        history.append(point)                   # recursive, not future data

    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["history window"] --> B["feature builder"]
    B --> C["fitted model<br>(weights in image)"]
    C --> D["point"]
    C --> E["residual quantiles"]
    D --> F["row h"]
    E --> F
    F --> G{"h < H?"}
    G -- yes --> H["append point to history"] --> B
    G -- no --> I["predictions frame"]

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I dark
```

<!-- Sources: src/model.py:89-114, src/series.py:136, src/series.py:221 -->

Two details decide whether this is honest:

- **Recursive or direct?** If you feed predictions back, say so in the card and
  docs; the benchmark horizon is multi-step, so future actuals are unavailable.
- **Where do quantiles come from?** Use the method's predictive distribution, or
  a held-out residual distribution. Do not invent a fixed width.

## Card changes come first

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["fdo.json"] --> B["config_schema<br>validates"]
    B --> C["run.py<br>passes parameters"]
    C --> D["your forecast()"]
    D --> E["tests<br>assert contract"]

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class A,B,C,D,E dark
```

<!-- Sources: fdo.json:31-67, src/config_schema.py:102-134 -->

For each new parameter, declare type, bounds, default and a description in
`episerve:parameters`. If it is the horizon, history or offset, add it to
`episerve:task.parameterRoles` so the benchmark workflow prefills it
([`fdo.json:24-28`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L24-L28)).
Update `tests/test_config_schema.py` in the same change; it is the guard that
keeps the card and the code from drifting.

If the method needs more runtime or memory, change `episerve:resources`. If it
needs network access or weights, set `network: true` and document why — the
default is an offline, self-contained image
([`fdo.json:111-117`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L111-L117)).

## Test the core, not the platform

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["hand-computed series"] --> B["test point values"]
    A --> C["test quantile ordering"]
    A --> D["test shape and columns"]
    E["same input twice"] --> F["test determinism"]
    G["constant / short / gappy series"] --> H["test edge cases"]
    I["max horizon"] --> J["test bound"]

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I,J dark
```

<!-- Sources: tests/test_model.py:22-135 -->

Keep the existing CLI tests untouched: they already prove the container contract
end to end ([`tests/test_run.py:153-170`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/tests/test_run.py#L153-L170)).
Add to `test_model.py` only what is specific to your method.

## Publish and register

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Dev as you
    participant CI as GitHub Actions
    participant GHCR as GHCR
    participant Runner as model-runner
    participant CKAN as CKAN

    Dev->>CI: push main / tag vX.Y.Z
    CI->>CI: validate fdo.json + pytest in image
    CI->>GHCR: push :latest / :vX.Y.Z
    Dev->>Runner: trigger run with image + config
    Runner-->>CKAN: first successful run registers the model
    Dev->>CKAN: add qualifying run to a benchmark
```

<!-- Sources: .github/workflows/publish.yml:17-83, README.md:151-160 -->

The first successful run is what creates the catalog entry; there is no manual
registration step. A benchmark entry additionally requires the run's provenance
to show exactly the benchmark input at the pinned commit.

## Anti-patterns

| Don't | Why it breaks |
|---|---|
| Re-read the parquet inside the core | Purity, testability, and the runner's window contract |
| Hardcode `datum` / `viruslast_normalisiert` | The model must work on any two-column series |
| Add parameters only in Python | The API rejects undeclared keys; the card is the contract |
| Train at inference | The benchmark measures forecasting, not fitting |
| Download weights at run time | `network: false`; non-reproducible runs |
| Use rows after the window | Future leakage; invalid benchmark entry |
| Return a fixed interval width | Coverage/interval score become meaningless |
| Ignore `maxHorizon` | OOM or timeout in Kubernetes |

Source: [`fdo.json:31-35`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L31-L35),
[`src/run.py:100-125`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/run.py#L100-L125),
[`README.md:164-172`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/README.md#L164-L172).

## Checklist

- [ ] Rename the image, repository and card `name`/`url`.
- [ ] Declare parameters, roles, resources and I/O in `fdo.json`.
- [ ] Replace `src/model.py`, keep the signature and output schema.
- [ ] Reuse `series.py` for axis and gaps.
- [ ] Add core tests; keep CLI, series and card tests green.
- [ ] Keep `ruff check src tests`, `mypy src` and coverage ≥ 95% green.
- [ ] Update `documentation/` and `README.md`.
- [ ] Build and run the container contract locally.
- [ ] Publish `:latest` and a pinned tag.
- [ ] Trigger one run; confirm the catalog entry.
- [ ] Add a benchmark entry with the pinned input.

For an agent-oriented, file-by-file brief, see
[`MODEL_TEMPLATE.md`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/MODEL_TEMPLATE.md).

<doc title="Documentation Index" path="index.md">
# model__prediction__generic__null-model

A dataset-agnostic **null forecaster** for the EPISERVE platform. It reads a time
series, computes one statistic of a trailing window (`mean`, `median` or
`last`), and writes that same value for every forecast step together with the
window's empirical 10th and 90th percentiles. It has no weights, no training, no
network access and no GPU — it is the performance floor that every real model
must beat, and a five-second end-to-end check of the model-runner pipeline
([`fdo.json:119-127`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/fdo.json#L119-L127)).

## Quick start

```bash
# 1. Install the two runtime dependencies plus pytest
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-test.txt

# 2. Put a config and a parquet file under ./work/input/
mkdir -p work/input work/output
cat > work/input/config.json <<'JSON'
{"history_length": 34, "prediction_length": 8, "statistic": "mean"}
JSON
# work/input/input.parquet: first column = time axis, second = target

# 3. Run
WORK_DIR=./work python src/run.py

# 4. Inspect
column -t -s $'\t' work/output/predictions.tsv
```

Expected shape for a numeric target `y`: one row per step, with `y`,
`y_q10` and `y_q90` constant across rows
([`src/model.py:106-114`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/model.py#L106-L114)).

## Architecture at a glance

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["config.json"] --> B["config_schema.validate_config"]
    C["input.parquet"] --> D["run.main: select window"]
    B --> D
    D --> E["series.prepare_target<br>fill gaps, reject long gaps"]
    D --> F["series.future_values<br>extrapolate x axis"]
    E --> G["model.forecast<br>point + q10/q90"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["predictions.tsv"]

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H dark
```

<!-- Sources: src/run.py:74, src/run.py:104-137, src/model.py:49-114, src/series.py:136, src/series.py:221 -->

The pipeline is deliberately linear: **validate → slice → prepare → forecast →
write**. There is no state between runs and no side channel
([`src/run.py:47-148`](https://github.com/The-EPISERVE-Consortium/model__prediction__generic__null-model/blob/main/src/run.py#L47-L148)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    I["documentation/index.md"] --> G["Getting Started"]
    I --> D["Deep Dive"]
    I --> O["Onboarding"]
    G --> G1["Overview / Contract / Config / Dev"]
    D --> D1["Pipeline / Series / Forecast / Card"]
    O --> O1["Contributor / Staff / Executive / PM"]

    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class I,G,D,O,G1,D1,O1 dark
```

## Tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Language | Python 3.11 | Matches the other EPISERVE model images |
| Data | pandas + pyarrow | Parquet input, TSV output |
| Numerics | NumPy | Mean, median and quantiles |
| Validation | jsonschema (Draft 2020-12) | The card is already a JSON Schema |
| Packaging | Docker, `python:3.11-slim` | Platform contract is a container |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions → GHCR | Build, test inside the image, push tags |
